classes.own-work: Written in this project (DnaCalc, or its own legacy repositories OxFunc, OxFml, OxCalc, DnaTreeCalc, DnaOneCalc, all MIT, DNA Kode). Includes rules and constants read from black-box Excel measurement, published mathematics (formulas, series, coefficients printed in papers and books) and the public x87/IEEE instruction set. Needs no notice.
classes.permissive-third-party: Code or data taken from a third party under a permissive licence; the entry names the licence and the notice a source or binary release carries.
classes.copyleft: Code or data whose licence would put copyleft terms on the file (GPL, LGPL); not compatible with presenting the file as MIT.
classes.proprietary-or-unclear: Code that follows a source whose terms forbid or restrict redistribution (Numerical Recipes) or whose terms for commercial redistribution are not settled (ACM Collected Algorithms, Applied Statistics algorithms).
classes.microsoft-derived: Content taken from Microsoft material: kind nt-source (the Windows NT/Server 2003 CRT source, 87tran.asm/87disp.asm/87cdisp.asm, a leaked copy), dll-disassembly (reading ucrtbase.dll machine code with dumpbin), documentation (support.microsoft.com pages: text, rules, examples).
classes.vendor-text: Prose copied from a vendor (here Microsoft's function descriptions).
classes.studied-reference: A port of a third-party implementation kept only to compare against; not reached by the product (test code or dead code).

DCDFLIB places its own work in the public domain but states that code from ACM publications stays subject to ACM's policy ('General permission to copy and distribute the algorithm without fee is granted provided that the copies are not made or distributed for direct commercial advantage'). files.reason: dc-j9k: J0/J1/Y0/Y1 low rational seeds, high polynomial seeds and adaptive J backward program from SheetJS/bessel bessel.js at 2e2331329891dc5c16bda3461db0b9fe590ff2e9, Apache-2.0; copyright, full licence and changes in deploy/notices/ported.txt. R27 high-J adapts a J0 decimal digit transposition and a repeated existing J1 amplitude term from original Excel phase-window observations; J0 retains its separate published phase table. Subsequent paired R25 phase observations support the common high J/Y ((8/x)*trig)*polynomial correction grouping with unchanged64/(x*x) reduction; all residual failures stay counted. The I0 and higher-I bodies additionally port ITK itkGaussianOperator.hxx at 311b7060ef39e371f3cd209ec135284ff5fde735, Apache-2.0, Copyright NumFOCUS, using existing stored PC64 operations; ITK NOTICE and changes are retained in deploy/notices/ported.txt.
